body:
## Why this exists

`sessionWindow: NULL` currently means **two opposite things at once**:

1. *"I deliberately allow this bot to act at any hour"* — the documented opt-in (`bot-rules.ts`: `NULL = ungated (opt-in)`)
2. *"nobody ever filled this slot in"*

Same value, opposite meanings, and no error either way.

Measured 2026-09-23 — three bots named for a session declare none:

| bot | name implies | `sessionWindow` |
|---|---|---|
| `Sydney AUDJPY Session` | asian | NULL |
| `GBPCAD Macro Session` | london | NULL |
| `Wellington NZDJPY Session` | asian | NULL |

Choosing all-hours deliberately and never filling the slot in are **indistinguishable**.

⚠️ This is the **same defect class as `strategyId = ''` vs NULL** (measured: 95,500 of 125,292 SCORED rows carry an empty string where NULL would be a different claim) — one value carrying two meanings, silently, with plausible output.

## The owner's framing (2026-09-23)

> *"maybe it could be hard-gate UNLESS a different rule is present to override it — I've visioned bots having standard slots for specific situations like this, every bot needing the slot filled even if it's a bypass/null/ignore/skip type rule."*

That is the right shape, and it has a **precedent already in this codebase**: `bot-rules.ts` documents `requireDirection` with the caveat that `role` on `strategy_protocol` **takes precedence**. A specific rule overriding a general one is an established pattern here, not a new invention.

## ⚠️ SEQUENCE — do this AFTER #981

#981 must run `auditNameVsWindow()` on **every** bot first. **Do not start this until it has produced the definitive list of NULL bots**, because:

1. Every NULL must be classified as **deliberate all-hours** or **never filled in**. That call cannot be made in the abstract — the list has to be in front of you.
2. A required-slot change applied first would **force a value to be written to satisfy a gate**. That is the fabrication class this repo keeps paying for: an invented default that exists only to make a validation pass.

## Scope

- Make the slot **declared**: a bot must state its session intent explicitly. `NULL` stops meaning "opt-in" and becomes "undecided".
- Provide an explicit **bypass / all-hours** value, so the deliberate case is expressible *and* distinguishable from an unfilled one.
- Every bot fills the slot — including "none / all hours / bypass" as a positive choice.
- Enforce it so the ambiguity cannot return. This is standing work and belongs with **#796**: `validate-bot-rules.cjs` already fails the build on an *undeclared* column; this adds *declared but unfilled*.
- Surface it on the bot view. **`ViewStrategyPage.jsx` already renders every declared rule with its value AND its enforcement status**, so a filled slot should appear there for free — **verify, do not rebuild**.
- Precedent worth reading before starting: **#977** (a capital allowance the rating requires, visible but writable only by API — a rule that exists without a surface).

## Not in scope
- The pre-open alert and the audit-on-every-tick — that is **#981**.
- The EXIT-side session gate — that is **#928**.
- Any change to the *set* of session tags, or to the session definitions themselves.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No bot can pass the build with an unfilled session slot — **canary it**: set one to NULL and show the gate fails
- [ ] A deliberate all-hours bot is expressible and clearly distinct from an unfilled one
- [ ] Every previously-NULL bot is classified with a recorded reason (deliberate vs filled in)
- [ ] The bot view shows a filled value for every bot, with no bot rendering an ambiguous blank
- [ ] Existing session behaviour is unchanged for bots that already declare a window — show before/after for one
- [ ] **Gate 3:** `npm --prefix nest run db:check` clean, `schema.prisma` updated **in the same commit**, and the NULL count before vs after pasted into the closing comment

## Related
- **#981** — prerequisite; produces the NULL list this depends on
- **#796** — standing work: make "this decision is unenforced" machine-checked
- **#977** — a rule visible but writable only by API
- **#870** — annotate create-bot fields with enforcement status
- **#851** / **#850** — session/market-hours consolidation, and the US-calendar gate
- **#934** — roadmap sprint **S3 — Time, sessions and exits**
- `nest/src/modules/trading/bot-rules.ts` — the registry (`sessionWindow` is `stage: 'entry'`, `enforcement: 'live'`)

comments.body:
Evidence from a whole-strategy audit (2026-10-06, bot "Tokyo EURJPY Session" + `forex-session-v1`).

**The same city resolves two ways across twin bots** — the NULL ambiguity this issue names is not only "unfilled vs deliberately all-hours"; it is *inconsistent between twins inside one protocol*:

| city in the name | gated twin | window | ungated twin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tokyo | USDJPY | `["asian"]` | EURJPY — NULL |
| Sydney | AUDUSD | `["asian"]` | AUDJPY — NULL |
| Wellington | NZDUSD | `["asian"]` | NZDJPY — NULL |
| Zurich | USDCHF | `["london"]` | EURCHF — NULL |

Plus 4 session-named bots ungated with no city word: EURCAD/GBPCAD "Macro Session", GBPUSD "Session", USDCAD "Forex Session".

`session-window.ts` (#759) records that the SEEDED city names meant the **news-flow** reading ("driven by Sydney news", not "the Sydney clock") — the same reading that made parenting them to a clock "the opposite of a fix". If that holds, the four GATED twins are enforcing a clock the name never meant; if the names meant clocks, the four NULL twins are unfilled. Either way the audit half (#981) should surface the **twin disagreement**, not only the per-bot "ungated" note — an operator reading one row cannot see that its sibling answers differently.

No trading hours were changed: the window is the owner's intent to declare, per #759's own rule ("report the question; do not answer it by editing the bot's trading hours"). Data source: `trading_strategy` (read 2026-10-06 ~20:30 UTC, all 40 active bots).

title: Make the bot session slot DECLARED - NULL currently means both 'deliberately all-hours' and 'nobody filled it in' (A, after #981)
